I’ll attach the E2E Long (experimental mode) graphs included in the pull request here for record-keeping.

I used the WMI model v7 (849aa9fb-dae6-4604-923e-050883def218) for about an hour.

It feels like the issue in WMI v6 where the car couldn’t maintain speed has been resolved 👍
However, about 10 minutes into the drive, the road started getting covered with snow, so I couldn’t test it properly at higher speeds. I’d like to see how it behaves again on a clear day.

As the comma team mentioned that this is the best world model so far, I was genuinely impressed that it could still recognize lanes and continue driving even on snowy roads. There was no behavior where the car got left behind by the vehicle in front; it followed smoothly even in those conditions.

Since road visibility was poor even for a human due to the snow, it felt like the car was driving slightly toward the right side of the lane. I’d also like to re-evaluate this on a clear day (I drive on Japanese roads, so I’d prefer it to stay slightly left).

I’ve been a long-time user of the Firehose model, but this WMI v7 feels like it could become a new gold standard model for me!

I don't really have a good reference for experimental and in dev's current state my car (2018 Clarity) can't accelerate well from a stop with a pedal installed. But it did seem to do a pretty decent job of maintaining speed although when it dropped below more than 7ish mph under the speed limit it seems like it had a difficult time recovering back to the set speed. 

Longitudinal felt really good and it was able to maintain center on par with DTRv6 imho although it did get a little close to the center line on sharp curves but I've only driven on it for about 30 minutes and it's probably not completely done calibrating considering the clarity is PID by default

I used this model today on the freeway, 20 minutes each way. It was perfectly acceptable, held the center of the lane, kept up with the traffic, made the curves with no problem. It slowed down (because of SLA I think) on the big exit ramp flyover and felt planted in the center of the lane where the stock Kia LFA always worried me so much that I wouldn't let it attempt that curve. The stock system always took the outside of the lane and with the concrete barriers close and knowing that the LFA might give up at any moment and the car would go straight, I just couldn't trust it.

I drove with WMI model v7 (849aa9fb-dae6-4604-923e-050883def218) for about 30 minutes during a clear daytime run.

The route was urban, but traffic was light and speeds reached around 70 km/h.
Centering performance was excellent—it consistently held the lane center in a very smooth and confidence-inspiring way. The WMI series has always impressed me with its lateral control, and WMI v7 clearly maintains that strength while also showing a big improvement in longitudinal behavior.

When there’s no lead car, it smoothly accelerates up to the speed limit. Even when the road ahead is clear, it correctly detects red lights, stops accelerating, and gently begins to decelerate toward the signal. The behavior feels very human-like.

The speed-holding issues seen in recent models seem to be resolved here. Overall, this feels like a very well-balanced model, and I’m planning to make WMI model v7 my new daily driver.

The main remaining challenge I see with WMI v7 is reliably stopping at red lights and stop signs.
Other than that, I honestly can’t think of any major issues 😆

Recently, after spending time with WMI v7, I’ve been thinking that in the Japanese road environment, expecting the system to perfectly understand everything is not very realistic.

Japan has many context-dependent traffic signals, such as red lights with directional arrows that allow movement in specific directions. Even for Japanese drivers who deeply understand local traffic culture, these can be confusing when encountered for the first time. Given that most of openpilot’s training data comes from the US, it’s understandable that these Japan-specific cases remain challenging.

Personally, rather than expecting perfect signal understanding from E2E longitudinal control, I think what matters most is:
* Maintaining a stable cruising speed while driving
* Naturally following and decelerating for a lead vehicle
* Falling back to safer behavior in uncertain situations
* Allowing easy and intuitive driver intervention when needed

If this balance is achieved, the system is already very practical for daily use.

In this regard, WMI v7 feels like a significant step forward. Its cruising and following behavior is highly refined. For now, letting humans handle Japan-specific edge cases while the car focuses on traffic flow and stability seems like the most realistic and effective approach.

This model is very inconsistent with stopping - it sees a vehicle in front but sometimes just ignores and continues accelerating. Very dangerous

Are you using Experimental Mode rather than Chill Mode?
In Chill Mode, the system does not proactively slow down far in advance when it detects a stopped vehicle. Its behavior is more conservative and may look like it’s continuing to accelerate until later. Experimental Mode generally handles stopped vehicles more predictively.

I think I am on the “mixed” mode.. But the current dev version does not really show what mode is currently active.  Experimental mode is unusable on the highways though, it goes really slow… So it’s more of a fight with acceleration than actually driving.
It not just “looks like”, it starts alarming about the crash and break now…

I’ve experienced this as well!
When using the mode where sunnypilot automatically switches between Chill and Experimental, I’ve seen cases where it approaches a stopped lead vehicle at a very high speed and doesn’t slow down properly, to the point where I had to brake manually to avoid a collision. This isn’t specific to WMI v7 — it’s a behavior I’ve noticed before.
A good workaround is to disable Dynamic Experimental Control via sunnylink.
If you enable Show Advanced Settings in User Preferences, you’ll see Dynamic Experimental Control appear under Cruise Settings.
Once that’s disabled, the behavior is much more predictable.
Also, WMI v7 is capable of accelerating sufficiently on highways, so it should feel much more comfortable after this change.
